_comment: Denver-Aurora-Centennial, CO MSA (CBSA 19740) - Adams, Arapahoe, Broomfield, Clear Creek, Denver, Douglas, Elbert, Gilpin, Jefferson and Park counties. AUTHORED FROM SCRATCH 2026-08-07: no metro config existed. GREENFIELD BY METRO_AREA BUT NOT EMPTY INSIDE THE ENVELOPE - see _stage_2b. Built under the v3 source-led coverage-first methodology including Stage 2c. NOT YET IMPORTED as of authoring.
_envelope_comment: Derived from the MSA COUNTY LIST, never from an observed bounding box. Union of the ten county OSM boundary-relation bboxes, rounded OUTWARD to 0.01 deg. Edges are driven by PARK county (latMin 38.6911, lngMin -106.2102), BROOMFIELD (latMax 40.0442) and ADAMS (lngMax -103.7056). Relations used: Adams 1411346, Arapahoe 1411351, Broomfield 1411321, Clear Creek 442310, Denver 1411339, Douglas 1411338, Elbert 1411319, Gilpin 1411333, Jefferson 1411327, Park 439376.
_envelope_consolidated_city_county_trap: TWO OF THE TEN COUNTY LOOKUPS RETURNED A WRONG BBOX, AND BOTH ARE CONSOLIDATED CITY-COUNTIES. Querying Nominatim for "<County> County, Colorado" works for eight counties. For DENVER it returns node/1362259731 - a POINT with a 0.01 deg box - and for BROOMFIELD it returns way/1530457347, a box roughly 180 m across. Neither is a boundary relation, and neither looks obviously wrong in a results list. THIS WAS NOT COSMETIC: Broomfield's true northern edge is lat 40.0442, NORTH of Adams' 40.0014, so Broomfield DRIVES latMax. Trusting the bad 180 m box would have set the envelope's north edge to 40.01 instead of 40.05 and silently shrunk the metro. Re-derived with "City and County of Denver, Colorado" and "City and County of Broomfield, Colorado", both of which return the correct boundary/administrative relation. RULE FOR THE NEXT METRO: whenever the county list contains a consolidated city-county (Denver, Broomfield, San Francisco, Philadelphia, Nashville, Indianapolis...), assert the Nominatim result is category=boundary AND type=administrative before using its bbox.
_envelope_overreach: KNOWN AND RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENTLY NARROWED. This MSA runs from the plains to the continental divide and the envelope is a rectangle, so it swallows a great deal. (1) COLORADO SPRINGS MSA (CBSA 17820, El Paso and Teller counties) is the largest over-reach and it is ALREADY BUILT AND LIVE - roughly 34 rows carrying metro_area "Colorado Springs" from batches colorado-springs-2026-08-03, colorado-springs-addendum-2026-08-03 and colorado-springs-v3-2026-08-05 sit inside this rectangle between lat 38.73 and 39.13. NOT ONE is touched by this build, and states:["CO"] fences none of them. (2) BOULDER MSA (CBSA 14500, Boulder County) occupies the northwest corner; four dormant OSM rows inside this envelope are Boulder County's. (3) GREELEY MSA (Weld County) contributes a southern sliver above Broomfield's latMax. (4) Mountain counties west of Park and Clear Creek (Summit, Lake, Chaffee, Fremont) clip the southwest corner. If an El Paso, Teller, Boulder or Weld row is ever admitted to this batch, tighten deliberately and name the row that forced it.
_prompt_inconsistency_resolved: THE TASK PROMPT CONTRADICTED ITSELF AND THIS BUILD RESOLVED IT AGAINST THE COUNTY LIST. The prompt states "Boulder is NOT in this MSA (own CBSA - exclude)", which is correct, and then names LOUISVILLE and LAFAYETTE in its municipal sweep - both of which are in BOULDER COUNTY, i.e. the Boulder MSA, not one of these ten counties. The ten-county list is authoritative, so Louisville, Lafayette, Erie and Superior are all excluded. This was corroborated against ground truth rather than assumed: the dormant OSM row "Relish" (way/61951748) carries a Louisville 80027 address and reverse-geocodes to Boulder County. Flagged for the owner rather than silently decided.

_require_all_geocoded_comment: false because 46 of the 94 venues carry a DELIBERATELY BLANK street address. Colorado municipalities and special districts overwhelmingly publish pickleball as a PROGRAM (schedules, drop-in times, fees) rather than as a FACILITY RECORD with a street address - Foothills Park & Recreation District names six outdoor parks with no address for any of them, and Apex Park and Recreation District names its facilities while giving only a district contact address that must not be assumed to be any one of them. Those rows reach only the name-based geocode rungs. A recalled address that is wrong is indistinguishable from a fabricated one, so each is expected to hold on "no coordinate" rather than publish a guessed pin. Every one is a lookup, not a research problem.
_stage_2b: UNION AGAINST THE DATABASE, RUN BEFORE ANY RECONCILES CLAIM WAS WRITTEN - the Detroit lesson applied deliberately rather than relearned. A metro_area query for Denver/Aurora/Centennial returns ZERO rows, which is what greenfield means; it is also BLIND to every metro_area IS NULL row, so it cannot see the dormant nationwide OSM ingest. The envelope-scoped sweep returned 16 such rows (status draft, source osm, verified_by NULL). FOUR are Boulder County's and are left untouched: Rex Ranch Pickleball Court (way/1391977980, reverse-geocodes to ERIE), Autrey Pickleball Court (way/852565469, SUPERIOR), Boulder Pickleball (node/13055499302) and Relish (way/61951748, LOUISVILLE). Rex Ranch and Autrey carry NO city, so neither could be classified without reverse-geocoding - and Rex Ranch sits at lat 40.0260, inside the corrected envelope but outside the broken one, so the Broomfield fix surfaced it for adjudication and the county check then correctly rejected it. TWELVE are in scope. ELEVEN of those became reconciles below. The twelfth is deliberately left dormant - see _generic_name_row.
_generic_name_row: ONE IN-SCOPE DORMANT ROW IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNTOUCHED: node/9063074711, named literally "Court", at 3000 South Ceylon Way, Aurora 80013 (slug "court-aurora-co"). It is almost certainly a real venue, but no non-aggregator source read in this build names it, and it CANNOT PUBLISH under that name in any case: publish-gate.mjs isGenericName strips court/tennis/pickleball words, so "Court" reduces to nothing and falls under the 3-character floor - the same mechanism that permanently blocked Boise's "S2 Pickleball". Renaming it would require a controlling-entity source this build did not find, and loosening isGenericName is out of the question because it is shared by both publish paths under ADR-17 and would change the gate for every metro. Left as a draft with verified_by NULL. Flagged for a completion pass, not for a gate change.
_metro_specific_instrument: COLORADO SPECIAL DISTRICTS ARE THE INSTRUMENT, AND THEY PAID OUT HEAVILY. Metropolitan districts and park-and-recreation districts are separate legal authorities from both the city and the county, each with its own facilities, and a city-only sweep is structurally blind to them. Venues in this batch that belong to a district rather than a municipality: SOUTH SUBURBAN PARKS AND RECREATION (SSIA Pickleball, the regional Sports Complex, Trails Recreation Center, Windermere Park, and half of Southpark), HIGHLANDS RANCH METRO DISTRICT (the other half of Southpark), FOOTHILLS PARK & RECREATION DISTRICT (Foothills Fieldhouse, Ridge and Lilley Gulch recreation centres, Clement Park and five more outdoor parks - nine venues from one district), APEX PARK AND RECREATION DISTRICT (Apex Center, Secrest Recreation Center, and the 24-court Marquardt-Miles complex) and HYLAND HILLS PARK & RECREATION DISTRICT (Clear Creek Valley Park). SOUTHPARK PICKLEBALL COMPLEX IS THE SHARPEST EXAMPLE: 19 courts, the largest single outdoor set in the metro, JOINTLY built and operated by two districts - South Suburban manages courts 1-10 and Highlands Ranch Metro District owns and manages 11-19 - and NEITHER OF THEM IS A CITY. Same structural class as Florida CDDs (Tampa), Michigan charter townships (Detroit) and the joint recreation authorities found in Detroit. Note the corollary: FOOTHILLS FIELDHOUSE CARRIES A DENVER MAILING ADDRESS but is Foothills district's facility, not the City of Denver's - a mailing address does not identify the controlling entity.
_stage_2c: THE UNAGGREGATED-VENUE PASS RAN. Found this way: country and racquet clubs (Cherry Creek Country Club, Club Greenwood, Denver Racquets Club, Colorado Athletic Club Monaco, Parker Racquet Club, Blackstone Country Club, Meadow Creek Tennis and Fitness Club, Racket Social Club), commercial clubs (Mile Hi Pickleball, The Picklr x3, Epic Pickleball Club x2, 3rd Shot Pickleball, Sporty Pickle, Ace Pickleball Club, Pickleball Food Pub x2, Chicken N Pickle, Life Time Flatirons), six YMCA of Metro Denver branches, and five 55+ / active-adult communities (Anthem Ranch, Skyestone, Hilltop at Inspiration, Fairway Villas at Green Valley Ranch, Stonegate Village). LOCAL EDITORIAL was again the top instrument: WESTWORD, Denver's alt-weekly, supplied most of the commercial layer with addresses. THE UNIVERSITY SUB-PASS RETURNED NOTHING - University of Denver, Metro State, Regis, Colorado School of Mines and CCD publish no pickleball court information any source read surfaces. That is the same null Detroit returned for its commuter universities and is recorded as a real negative, not a skipped instrument.
_thin_counties: FOUR OF THE TEN COUNTIES ARE GENUINELY THIN AND CONTRIBUTE NOTHING TO THIS BATCH: CLEAR CREEK (Idaho Springs, Georgetown), GILPIN (Black Hawk, Central City), PARK (Bailey, Fairplay) and ELBERT (Elizabeth, Kiowa). These are mountain and plains counties with populations in the low thousands; searches returned no citable non-aggregator pickleball venue in any of them. This is a FINDING, not a gap - reported the way Boise reported Kuna. Between them these four counties hold roughly 1.5% of the MSA population while occupying well over half its land area, which is also why the envelope is so much larger than the populated core.
